title: Revelation 2:12–17
context: Pergamum lives where Satan’s throne is, yet it held to Christ’s name even when Antipas was killed. But some in the church follow the teaching of Balaam and the Nicolaitans. Christ calls them to repent and promises the overcomer hidden manna and a white stone with a new name.

verses.text: “To the angel of the assembly in Pergamum write: “He who has the sharp two-edged sword says these things:
verses.arminianNotes: The sharp two-edged sword is Christ’s word of judgment, which will be turned against false teaching if the church does not repent.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see Christ’s word as the instrument by which he rules and judges his church.

verses.text: “I know your works and where you dwell, where Satan’s throne is. You hold firmly to my name, and didn’t deny my faith in the days of Antipas my witness, my faithful one, who was killed among you, where Satan dwells.
verses.arminianNotes: Satan’s throne may refer to the city’s emperor worship, its great altar, or its role as a seat of Roman authority. The church held fast even when Antipas died. Arminian readers see faithfulness Christ honors.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see faith preserved in a hostile setting. Antipas is called “my faithful one,” a title Christ shares with him (1:5).

verses.text: But I have a few things against you, because you have there some who hold the teaching of Balaam, who taught Balak to throw a stumbling block before the children of Israel, to eat things sacrificed to idols, and to commit sexual immorality.
verses.arminianNotes: The teaching of Balaam refers to Numbers 25 and 31:16, where Israel was led into idolatry and immorality. Some in Pergamum were tolerating similar compromise.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note the danger of tolerating teaching that blends faith with idolatry. Church discipline is part of faithfulness.

verses.text: So also you likewise have some who hold to the teaching of the Nicolaitans.
verses.arminianNotes: The Nicolaitans seem to have taught a similar compromise. Arminian readers see a warning against teaching that excuses sin.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see the church’s duty to guard both doctrine and life.

verses.text: Repent therefore, or else I am coming to you quickly and I will make war against them with the sword of my mouth.
verses.arminianNotes: The call to repent is addressed to the whole church, not only to the false teachers. Arminian readers see the conditional threat as a real summons to respond.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see Christ’s threat as a means of purifying his church. He will fight the false teachers with his word.

verses.text: He who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the assemblies. To him who overcomes, to him I will give of the hidden manna, and I will give him a white stone, and on the stone a new name written which no one knows but he who receives it.
verses.arminianNotes: The hidden manna recalls God’s provision in the wilderness, and the white stone may refer to admission tokens or acquittal verdicts. The new name speaks of personal belonging to Christ.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see the new name as a sign of Christ’s personal knowledge of each of his people. The overcomer receives intimacy with him that no one else can share.
